evidence_summary: Milled endosperm of wheat grain with bran and germ removed. Contains gluten proteins (gliadin & glutenin). High carbohydrate, low fiber.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Wheat Flour (CXS 152-1985)
notes: Universal staple in biscuits, bakery goods, and instant noodles. Contains Gluten.

evidence_summary: Ground dried maize kernels. Naturally gluten-free grain rich in carotenoids (lutein, zeaxanthin) and complex carbohydrates.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Degermed Maize Meal and Maize Grits (CXS 155-1985)
notes: Base ingredient in corn puffs, tortilla chips, and breakfast cereals.

evidence_summary: Whole cereal grain rich in soluble fiber (arabinoxylans) with low glycemic response. Contains gluten (secalin protein).
source_reference: 21 CFR 137.250 (FDA Rye Flour Standard)
notes: Key flour in European crispbreads, rye bread, and multigrain crackers.

evidence_summary: Pseudocereal containing all nine essential amino acids. Naturally gluten-free, rich in iron, magnesium, and quercetin flavonoids.
source_reference: Codex Regional Standard for Quinoa (CXS 333R-2020)
notes: Used in healthy snack crisps, protein bars, and baby cereals.

evidence_summary: Richest plant source of calcium (~344 mg/100g, 3x more than milk). High dietary fiber, polyphenol antioxidants, and low glycemic index.
source_reference: International Year of Millets (IYM 2023) / FSSAI Millet Standards
notes: Signature nutri-cereal in Indian health cookies, baby foods, and malt drinks.

evidence_summary: Drought-hardy cereal exceptionally rich in iron and zinc. High protein, slowly digestible starch.
source_reference: FSSAI Food Product Standards for Millets
notes: Present in multigrain chips, khakhra, and health cookies.

evidence_summary: Rich in anthocyanin and tannin polyphenols. Gluten-free, supports gut health and glycemic control.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Sorghum Grains (CXS 172-1989)
notes: Widely used in puffed sorghum snacks and gluten-free flour mixes.

evidence_summary: Cooked, mashed, and drum-dried potatoes. High in digestible carbohydrates and potassium. Gluten-free.
source_reference: 21 CFR 182.1625 (FDA GRAS Potato Starch)
notes: Dominant ingredient in stacked potato crisps and extruded savouries.

evidence_summary: Randomly bonded condensation polymer of glucose with sorbitol and citric acid. Safe prebiotic soluble fiber with low glycemic effect.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 1200 (ADI not specified)
notes: Common in 'high-fiber' or 'sugar-free' cookies, energy bars, and yogurts.

evidence_summary: Sucrose crystals retaining natural cane molasses (3–7%). Classified as free sugar by WHO.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Sugars (CXS 212-1999)
notes: Found in chocolate chip cookies, premium cakes, and barbecue sauces.

evidence_summary: Monosaccharide with sweetness 1.7x of sucrose. Low initial glycemic index (GI ~19), but excessive intake metabolized exclusively in liver, linked to hepatic lipogenesis.
source_reference: 21 CFR 184.1857 (FDA GRAS)
notes: Used in sports drinks, fruit snack gummies, and low-GI baked goods.

evidence_summary: Hydrogenated glucose polyol. Safe, tooth-friendly (non-cariogenic). Caution: Excessive consumption (>20g/day) may cause mild laxative effects.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 420 (ADI not specified)
notes: Universal in chewing gums, mints, and sugar-free confectionery.

evidence_summary: Polyol derived from maltose. Half the calories of sugar (2.1 kcal/g), minimal insulin demand. Non-cariogenic.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 965 (ADI not specified)
notes: Prime sweetener in 'zero sugar' chocolates and diabetic cookies.

evidence_summary: Naturally occurring 4-carbon polyol. 90% absorbed in small intestine and excreted unchanged in urine; does not ferment in colon or spike blood sugar.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 968 (ADI not specified / FDA GRAS)
notes: Leading sweetener in keto foods, diet drinks, and low-carb chocolate.

evidence_summary: Dipeptide methyl ester (aspartic acid + phenylalanine). JECFA reaffirmed safe consumption within ADI (40 mg/kg bw). Mandatory warning: 'Contains Phenylalanine' for PKU patients.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 951 (ADI 0–40 mg/kg bw, JECFA/WHO 2023 evaluation)
notes: Present in Diet Coke, chewing gums, sugar-free jelly, and yogurts.

evidence_summary: Potassium salt of 6-methyl-1,2,3-oxathiazine-4(3H)-one 2,2-dioxide. Highly heat stable, excreted unchanged. Safe within ADI.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 950 (ADI 0–15 mg/kg bw)
notes: Widely blended with sucralose or aspartame in zero-sugar soft drinks.

evidence_summary: Liquid fraction obtained by fractionation of palm oil. Rich in oleic acid (MUFA) and tocotrienols. Contains ~45% saturated fatty acids (palmitic acid).
source_reference: Codex Standard for Named Vegetable Oils (CXS 210-1999)
notes: The #1 frying oil used in packaged potato chips, bhujia, sev, and instant noodles.

evidence_summary: Low saturated fat (<7%), high in monounsaturated fats (oleic acid ~61%) and plant Omega-3 (ALA ~11%). Authorized FDA qualified health claim for heart disease risk reduction.
source_reference: 21 CFR 184.1555c (FDA Canola Oil Health Claim)
evidence_status: Approved Food Standard with Health Claim
notes: Used in premium mayonnaise, dressings, and baked snack crackers.

evidence_summary: Extracted from the outer brown layer (bran) of rice. Naturally rich in Gamma-Oryzanol (antioxidant that helps lower LDL cholesterol) and balanced MUFA/PUFA.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Named Vegetable Oils (CXS 210-1999)
notes: Popular healthy frying oil in modern chips and extruded snacks.

evidence_summary: Extremely rich in monounsaturated fatty acids (oleic acid >70%) and polyphenol antioxidants (oleocanthal, hydroxytyrosol). EFSA validated health claims for cardiovascular protection.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Olive Oils (CXS 33-1981)
evidence_status: Approved Food Standard with Authorized Health Claim
notes: Present in gourmet crackers, pesto, pasta sauces, and potato chips.

evidence_summary: Rich in sesamin and sesamolin lignans. Caution: Sesame is classified as a major food allergen under the US FASTER Act (2023) and EU allergen laws.
source_reference: Codex Standard CXS 210-1999
notes: Common in Asian instant noodles, chilli oils, and savory crackers.

evidence_summary: Water-in-oil emulsion of vegetable fats (minimum 80% fat). Modern regulations (WHO REPLACE initiative & FSSAI) mandate industrial trans-fatty acids <=2% of total fat.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Fat Spreads and Blended Spreads (CXS 256-2007)
notes: Universal fat in packaged puff pastries, flaky biscuits, and cookies.

evidence_summary: Pure ground cocoa nibs containing ~53% cocoa butter and ~47% cocoa solids. Dense in flavanol polyphenols (epicatechin) supporting vascular health.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Chocolate and Chocolate Products (CXS 87-1981)
notes: Core constituent of authentic dark and milk chocolate bars.

evidence_summary: Formulated with cocoa solids, sugar, vegetable fats, and emulsifier (INS 322). Contributes to total added sugar and fat content.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Chocolate and Chocolate Products (CXS 87-1981)
notes: Universal in chocolate chip cookies (Hide & Seek, Good Day Choco-chip, etc.).

evidence_summary: Dried unripe fruit of Piper nigrum containing alkaloid piperine (which significantly increases absorption of curcumin and other nutrients).
source_reference: Codex Standard for Black, White and Green Peppers (CXS 326-2017)
notes: Key seasoning in salt & pepper wafers, savory biscuits, and soup powders.

evidence_summary: Ground seeds of Coriandrum sativum rich in linalool essential oil and dietary fiber. Digestive stimulant.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Coriander Seeds (CXS 342-2021)
notes: Universal foundation spice in namkeen seasonings and instant noodle tastemakers.

evidence_summary: Dried seeds of Cuminum cyminum containing cuminaldehyde. Stimulates pancreatic digestive enzymes.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Cumin (CXS 327-2017)
notes: Signature spice in 50-50 Maska Chaska, Jeera biscuits, and savory chips.

evidence_summary: Dried rhizome containing gingerols and shogaols with validated anti-inflammatory and digestive benefits.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Dried Ginger (CXS 343-2021)
notes: Present in ginger cookies, chai premixes, and Asian snack seasonings.

evidence_summary: Dried inner bark containing cinnamaldehyde. Clinically proven to support blood glucose metabolism.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Cinnamon
notes: Essential in cinnamon toast crunch cereals, buns, and spiced biscuits.

evidence_summary: Elettaria cardamomum seeds containing cineole and terpinyl acetate. Natural breath freshener and digestive stimulant.
source_reference: Codex Standard for Cardamom
notes: Iconic spice in Parle-G Elaichi, Good Day, and traditional mithai.

evidence_summary: Sodium salt of inosinic acid (natural purine nucleotide). Evaluated as safe by JECFA/EFSA. Note: Individuals with hyperuricemia or gout should moderate purine intake.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 631 (ADI not specified)
notes: Almost always paired with MSG and Guanlyate in noodle tastemakers and potato chips.

evidence_summary: Sodium salt of guanylic acid. Evaluated as safe by JECFA. Functions synergistically with glutamates.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 627 (ADI not specified)
notes: Standard ingredient in Doritos, Lays, Maggi tastemakers, and savory bouillons.

evidence_summary: Equal parts disodium inosinate and disodium guanylate. Safe at technological usage levels.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 635 (ADI not specified)
notes: Present in savory chips, instant noodles, and ready-to-eat gravies.

evidence_summary: Esters of mono- and diglycerides with tartaric and acetic acids. Essential dough conditioner in commercial baking.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 472e (ADI 0–50 mg/kg bw)
notes: Present in sandwich breads, burger buns, crackers, and cream biscuits.

evidence_summary: Sodium salt of the stearic acid ester of lactylic acid. Fully metabolized into stearic acid and lactic acid.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 481(i) (ADI 0–20 mg/kg bw)
notes: Standard ingredient in packaged breads, tortillas, and snack cakes.

evidence_summary: High-molecular weight sulfated galactan extracted from red edible seaweeds. Food-grade carrageenan is non-degraded and fully cleared by JECFA/EFSA.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 407 (ADI not specified, JECFA 2015)
notes: Universal stabilizer in chocolate milk, almond milk, and vegan desserts.

evidence_summary: Heteropolysaccharide extracted from citrus peel and apple pomace. Wholesome soluble fiber that helps moderate cholesterol and gut transit.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 440 (ADI not limited)
notes: Primary gelling agent in fruit jams, jellies, gummy candies, and fruit yogurts.

evidence_summary: Cellulose ether derivative. Physiologically inert, non-absorbable dietary fiber.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 466 (ADI not specified)
notes: Present in sauces, ice creams, diet drinks, and bakery icings.

evidence_summary: Potassium salt of sorbic acid (unsaturated fatty acid). Metabolized by the human body like dietary fatty acids into CO2 and water. Very safe.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 202 (ADI 0–11 mg/kg bw expressed as sorbic acid)
notes: Universal preservative in packaged cakes, cheese slices, fruit sauces, and dried fruits.

evidence_summary: Calcium salt of propionic acid (short-chain fatty acid produced naturally in gut microbiome). Safe, non-toxic.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 282 (ADI not limited)
notes: Present in virtually every packaged commercial sandwich bread and bun worldwide.

evidence_summary: Synthetic phenolic antioxidant. Strict concentration limits (<=200 mg/kg fat) enforced by FSSAI and FDA.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 320 (ADI 0–0.5 mg/kg bw)
notes: Used in potato chips, namkeen, dry cereal mixes, and chewing gums.

evidence_summary: Synthetic phenolic antioxidant. Safe within regulated ADI limits.
source_reference: Codex GSFA INS 321 (ADI 0–0.25 mg/kg bw)
notes: Added to breakfast cereal liners, dehydrated potato flakes, and snacks.

evidence_summary: Primary flavor component of vanilla bean (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde). Evaluated by JECFA with ADI 0–10 mg/kg bw. Fully safe.
source_reference: 21 CFR 182.60 (FDA GRAS)
notes: Present in almost all vanilla wafers, ice creams, biscuits, and chocolates.

evidence_summary: Essential fat-soluble vitamin. Crucial for normal vision, gene expression, and immune integrity. Mandated in fortified edible oils.
source_reference: FSSAI Mandatory Fortification Standards (+F logo)
notes: Standard fortification in edible oils, milk, and health food drinks.

evidence_summary: Fat-soluble secosteroid essential for intestinal absorption of calcium, magnesium, and phosphate. Combats rickets and osteomalacia.
source_reference: FSSAI Fortification Regulations
notes: Added to fortified milk, plant milks, cereal flakes, and malt beverages.

evidence_summary: Crucial trace mineral preventing iron deficiency anemia (affecting >50% of children/women in developing nations).
source_reference: WHO Guidelines on Food Fortification with Micronutrients
notes: Key fortificant in fortified wheat flour (Atta), breakfast cereals, and Bournvita/Horlicks.
